author: sket88
title: [Mouse Without Borders] v0.101.2652.0: Settings rejects MWB with "Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature" because Settings.exe and MWB binaries are signed with different certificates

status.label: Actionable fix hypothesis
status.detail: The reporter's signer-mismatch evidence matches the verifier's full leaf-certificate equality check; the newer release claim still needs package verification.

next_action.label: Reproduce MWB signer mismatch
next_action.reason: Verify the reported 0.101.2652.0 package and the added 0.101.2684.0 ARM64 report before selecting a constrained signer policy or release-signing correction.

judgment.rationale: The detailed report gives exact signer thumbprints, valid signature/chain claims, the repeated untrusted-signature error, and a source method that compares signer RawData byte-for-byte. The new comment says the same issue occurs on 0.101.2684.0 machine-wide ARM64, but does not provide signer identities or a fresh log for that build. PR #50480 is merged and introduced verification; open draft PR #49949 is the general feature, not a demonstrated fix for this release signer split. Preserve strict trust and process checks; do not infer that subject-only matching is safe.
evidence: The issue reproduces on 0.101.2652.0 per-user x64 in both MWB service and user modes, with Settings logging `Rejected SettingsSync server: untrusted-signature`.
The reporter lists Settings/PowerToys signer AB172913A2960A224809EE8A0C371CD47A079B72 and MWB signer 1D77A9B9E8FE2075D9AD15123257FB90DB0DA4A1, and says both signatures and chains are valid.
The report says the same installed release has 371 files signed with one thumbprint and 196 with the other, while 0.101.2362.0 used the same signer for Settings and MWB and worked.
The latest comment adds reproduction on 0.101.2684.0 machine-wide ARM64 and says an x64 machine can connect to a 0.101.2632.0 ARM64 machine.

Current artifact code review identifies NamedPipePeerVerification.MeetsSigningPolicy/HaveSameTrustedMicrosoftSigner/HaveMatchingSignerCertificate as the relevant path; PR #50480 is merged, PR #49949 remains an open draft, and issue #50615 is a distinct revocation failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact signer split on both reported packages, then design either a tightly constrained release-signer relationship or a release-signing correction while preserving signature, executable, and peer-identity checks.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current peer-verification check rejects distinct leaf certificates even when each reported signer is a trusted Microsoft signer; no open or merged fix found covers the specific release signer split.

proposed_fixes.title: Handle the reported Microsoft release-signer split without weakening peer authentication
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The settings-sync verifier requires byte-identical leaf signer certificates after separately validating Microsoft signing, so distinct valid release signers within communicating PowerToys binaries are rejected.
plan: Verify signatures, signer identities, and SettingsSync rejection on the exact 0.101.2652.0 x64 package and the newly reported 0.101.2684.0 machine-wide ARM64 package.

Confirm whether release policy guarantees one signer per package; if not, replace unconditional leaf equality only with an explicitly constrained trusted-signer relationship, or correct signing so mutually communicating binaries use a compatible signer.
Add tests for approved distinct release signers and rejection of untrusted signers, invalid signatures, wrong executable identity, and wrong process identity.
Validate New key and peer synchronization with service mode enabled and disabled on the final signed packages.
verification: Run focused settings-sync identity tests for two distinct approved signers and negative cases.
Reproduce New key and connection on the official package in both service modes.
Confirm invalid or untrusted peers remain rejected.

confidence.rationale: The original report's signer values and the byte-equality check align directly; the new package report lacks signer details, and release policy must determine the safe correction.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders Settings rejects the MWB process in a release where the reporter says its Microsoft signing leaf certificate differs from Settings.exe.
known_information: The original report provides exact signer thumbprints, the repeated untrusted-signature error, Windows 11 build numbers, and service-on/off behavior.
The reporter says both signatures are valid and that 0.101.2362.0 worked when the binaries shared a signer.
The newest comment reports the same symptom on 0.101.2684.0 machine-wide ARM64, without adding that build's signer identities.
PR #50480 is merged; PR #49949 remains an open draft; #50615 concerns a different revocation failure.
inferences: The exact 0.101.2652.0 rejection is likely caused by the verifier's full leaf-certificate equality requirement if the reported package signatures are confirmed.
The new ARM64 report may share that mechanism, but its certificate details have not been supplied.
issue_context.analysis: The original issue already contains enough diagnostic evidence to avoid asking for generic logs. A maintainer-side reproduction can verify the newer package claim and determine whether release-signing policy or a narrow trust rule is appropriate. Comparing only certificate subject or issuer would be broader than the evidence supports.
initial_investigation: Read the live body, sole comment, labels, assignees, and timeline; no author-wait label or issue-linked fix is present.
Checked current live state of PR #50480 (merged), PR #49949 (open draft), and issue #50615 (open, distinct revocation path).
The prior v5 artifact's source inspection identifies the peer verification methods and full RawData comparison; this judgment preserves that evidence and refreshes the newer comment.

actions.label: Approve constrained MWB signer-policy design
actions.note: This starts a fork-side design investigation; it does not authorize or claim an upstream change.

reproduce.title: Verify release signer identities and settings-sync rejection
reproduce.version_requirement: Official signed 0.101.2652.0 per-user x64 package; also verify the reporter's 0.101.2684.0 machine-wide ARM64 package and 0.101.2632.0 ARM64 peer claim if available.
prerequisites: Use Windows 11 and the official signed packages.
Test MWB with Use Service enabled and disabled.
setup: Record Authenticode signature validity and signer thumbprints for Settings.exe, PowerToys.exe, and the MWB/service binaries in each package.
steps: Open Settings > Mouse Without Borders and click New key.
Attempt to connect to another machine and check whether settings synchronization succeeds.
Repeat with Use Service on and off.
Compare signer thumbprints and the SettingsSync rejection in the PowerToys report.
reproduce.expected_result: Determine whether the exact release packages contain distinct valid signers and whether that difference causes rejection, without accepting an untrusted peer.
